bandReport.notes:
29 questions, Q35-Q63 contiguous, no gaps. Page mapping: p06 = printed (13-A) Q35-40; p07 = (15-A) Q41-46; p08 = (17-A) Q47-55; p09 = (19-A) Q56-63. Note the render skips the Hindi versos, so PNG index N == PDF page N == printed odd page 2N+1.

BAND EDGES — Q35 opens the left column of p06 with its number and full stem; nothing continues from p05, so B1 should end at Q34. Q63 closes the right column of p09 with option (d) 'Core service' immediately above the footer; nothing spills to p10, so B3 should open at Q64.

NO shared 'Directions:' block and NO shared code block anywhere in this band. Every question carries its own four options in its own column. No Match Lists, so no pipe tables were needed. Six 'Consider the following statements' items (Q36, Q42, Q46, Q61) have their numbered statements folded into the stem per Rule 2.

SUBJECT BOUNDARIES inside the band (useful for the merge): History Q35-Q50; Chemistry Q51-Q60; Economics Q61-Q63. The History->Chemistry switch happens mid-page at the top of p08's right column, and the Chemistry->Economics switch mid-page at the top of p09's right column.

ITALICS: the page italicises transliterated terms and work titles (Zainavilas, manjaniq, ishukrit, isukara, yakshi, Ain-i Akbari, and all four options of Q41/Q48/Q49 plus Q37(c) Vajra). These are typographic convention, not meaning-changing emphasis, so they are transcribed as plain text. The bold-italic 'not' in Q35/Q38/Q52/Q58 IS load-bearing and is kept as **not**.

All option blocks were re-checked against the page at 7-8x crops after first transcription (Rule 1), with individual crops taken for every question carrying chemical formulae, proper nouns or work titles: Q37, Q38, Q39, Q41, Q44, Q45, Q47, Q48, Q49, Q51, Q52, Q53, Q54, Q56, Q59, Q60, Q61, Q62.

CATALOG GAP (4 questions): there is no subtopic anywhere under History for MILITARY TECHNOLOGY / ARMS AND WARFARE. Q36 (stirrup), Q38 (names for the bow), Q39 (manjaniq siege engine) and Q42 (European muskets, bayonets, cannon) all test it, and this paper evidently sets it as a recurring theme. Each is filed under the closest available chapter subtopic and flagged.

NO page defects found: no missing options, no duplicated options, no impossible values, nothing illegible. Print quality is good throughout; Hindi verso bleed-through is visible but never obscures the English text.
